steps.en: What you see: Colour shows a diastolic jet from aorta to ventricle starting at the valve. The left ventricle dilates and beats with hyperdynamic motion early in the disease. Severe disease gives a vena contracta of 6 mm or more with a short pressure half time below 200 ms. Holodiastolic flow reversal in the descending aorta confirms severe regurgitation when present.

Normal values with units: Effective regurgitant orifice. Mild below 0.10 sq cm. Moderate 0.10 to 0.29 sq cm. Severe 0.30 sq cm or more.. Source: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on aortic regurgitation quantitation
Regurgitant volume. Mild below 30 ml. Moderate 30 to 59 ml. Severe 60 ml or more per beat.. Source: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on aortic regurgitation quantitation
Vena contracta width. Mild below 3 mm. Severe 6 mm or more at the narrowest neck.. Source: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on vena contracta

Pressure half time. Below 200 ms marks severe disease in the acute setting with a steep deceleration slope.. Source: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on aortic regurgitation quantitation

ECG and heart sound correlation ecg: Left ventricular hypertrophy follows the volume pattern with tall R waves. Left axis deviation appears with chronic disease. T wave flattening in lateral leads warns of dysfunction setting in.

ECG and heart sound correlation sounds: An early diastolic decrescendo murmur at the left sternal edge marks the leak. The first sound softens and a third sound marks severe chronic disease. An Austin Flint rumble at the apex mimics mitral stenosis in severe disease.

What to report: Jet width ratio, vena contracta, effective orifice and regurgitant volume with blood pressure
Pressure half time with the envelope quality and descending aorta reversal
Cavity diameters, volumes and ejection fraction against surgical thresholds
Aortic root and ascending size with cusp number and any prolapse or vegetation
Red flags needing urgent referral: Acute severe regurgitation with pulmonary oedema after dissection or endocarditis, needs emergency surgical review
Severe chronic disease with ejection fraction 55 percent or below or end systolic diameter above 50 mm, needs prompt surgical review
Dilated ascending aorta with a diastolic murmur, needs urgent aortopathy review for dissection risk
Pitfalls: Rheumatic aortic disease often travels with mitral disease in Indian patients, so examine every valve in every study.
A short pressure half time also follows a stiff non compliant aorta, so integrate jet size and reversal.
Acute severe disease keeps a small cavity with high pressure, so normal size never rules out severe acute leak.
Figure: Apical five chamber view lines up continuous wave Doppler for pressure half time and descending aorta flow for reversal. View tte_a5c

todo.en: How to get it on the probe, step by step: Start in the parasternal long axis and map the diastolic jet with colour across the valve.
Measure jet width against outflow tract height just below the valve.
Record continuous wave Doppler through the jet and measure the pressure half time.
Move to the suprasternal window and record descending aorta flow for holodiastolic reversal.
Measure left ventricular diameters and volumes for dilatation and function.

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Grading from one view where the jet looks deceptively short. Fix: Measure in the view where the jet looks longest and confirm from a second window before grading.
Reading pressure half time from a faint incomplete trace. Fix: Shorten the half time reading only from a complete dense envelope, since faint traces underread.
Ignoring blood pressure which changes the jet within minutes. Fix: Record blood pressure with every study and repeat when controlled, since grade follows pressure.

remember.en: Separate acute from chronic patterns and time surgical referral.

q.en: Which pair marks severe aortic regurgitation?

o.en: 0.30 sq cm or more with 60 ml or more
Any visible jet regardless of size

why.en: Severe needs effective orifice 0.30 sq cm or more with regurgitant volume 60 ml or more.

q.en: Which Doppler sign confirms severe disease?

o.en: Holodiastolic reversal in the descending aorta

why.en: Flow reversal through the whole of diastole in the descending aorta is a specific severe sign.

q.en: Which pattern is a surgical emergency?

o.en: Chronic severe jet with a hugely dilated compliant ventricle
Acute severe leak with pulmonary oedema and a near normal cavity

why.en: Acute severe regurgitation gives a small stiff ventricle no time to adapt, so pulmonary oedema follows fast.

q.en: Blood pressure is 190 over 110 during the study. What do you do?

o.en: Record pressure and repeat when controlled before final grading
Ignore pressure because jets never change

why.en: Grade follows pressure within minutes, so record it and repeat the study when pressure is controlled.
